title: Visser’s anti-diagonal normalization theorem

based_on.title: Generalizations of the recursion theorem
based_on.pages: 1683–1690; author manuscript dated 2019-12-16, section 3 Theorems 3.1 and 3.3, pp.3–4

summary: Use parameterized self-reference to totalize partial index-valued computations while avoiding a partial fixed-point-free transformation.
abstract: An algorithm can return a program index even when another computation never returns one. Totalization asks the returned index to describe the requested domain whenever that request is defined. Visser’s anti-diagonal normalization theorem adds an avoidance condition: a partial computable transformation that never returns an index for its own input domain must remain undefined on the selected indices of undefined requests. A first-arrival race and parameterized self-reference construct a primitive-recursive selector. A winning avoidance branch would make its own domain a forbidden fixed point, so every successful race copies the requested program. One universal request gives a selector for all partial computable requests, and simple examples distinguish domain agreement from agreement of returned output values.
